sections.content:
Very suggestive! When I clicked the cross at (r1,c2) (19,24):
1. The G selection ring moved from c1 to c2 (the cross at c1 is now back to normal, and c2 has the ring).
2. The g plus at c3 disappeared.
3. A new g plus appeared at c0 (rows 18-21, cols 11-14): (18,12),(18,13),(19,11),(19,14),(20,11),(20,14),(21,12),(21,13) — same plus shape, now on the leftmost block c0.
So the pattern is: the gray plus appears on the block that is 2 columns to the left of the selected cross? Selection is at c1 → plus at c3 (2 to the right). Selection is at c2 → plus at c0 (2 to the left). Hmm, not consistent.
Wait: selection c1 → plus c3; selection c2 → plus c0. Differences: +2 and -2. Hmm. Or maybe the plus appears on the block that is "2 away" in the direction of the nearest edge? c1 is 1 from the left edge, 5 from the right; c2 is 2 from the left, 4 from the right. Hmm.
Or: the plus appears on the block that is 2 away in the direction of the nearest cross? From c1, the nearest other cross is c2 (distance 1)... no.
Another idea: maybe the plus is placed at the position of the "mirror" of the selected cross... c1→c3, c2→c0. Hmm, c1+c3 = 4, c2+c0 = 2. No.
Maybe the plus is placed on the block that is 2 to the left of the selection, wrapping around? c1-2 = -1 → wrap to c6? No, it was at c3.
Maybe the plus indicates where the cross will "jump" when ACTION7 is pressed? Or the plus is a "shot" trajectory: the cross fires 2 blocks in some direction?
Wait a sec. Let me reconsider: maybe the plus is placed on the block that is 2 away in the direction of the last movement? I clicked c1 first (no movement), plus at c3 (+2). Then clicked c2, plus at c0 (-2). Hmm, direction from c1 to c2 is -1... plus is -2?
Or maybe the plus is placed on the block that is 2 away in the direction of the nearest empty block? From c1: the nearest empty block is c0 (distance 1) or c3 (distance 2, since c2 has a cross). Plus appeared at c3. From c2: the nearest empty is c0 (distance 2, c1 has a cross... wait, c1 has a cross). Empty blocks in row 1: c0, c3, c5, c6. From c2: nearest empty is c3 (distance 1) or c0 (distance 2). Plus appeared at c0, not c3. Hmm, no.
Maybe the plus is placed on the block that is 2 away in the direction of the nearest cross? From c1: nearest cross is c2 (distance 1, rightward); 2 in that direction → c3. ✓. From c2: nearest cross is c1 (distance 1, leftward); 2 in that direction → c0. ✓!!
So the plus appears 2 blocks away from the selected cross, in the direction of the nearest other cross. Interesting — this looks like a "reflection" or "projection" mechanic.
Or more simply: the plus is placed at the position of "selected cross + 2*(direction to nearest cross)".
Hmm, what's the purpose? Maybe the goal is to make the plus land on a block that has a cross? Or to eliminate the cross by firing the plus? If I select a cross such that the plus lands on another cross... For example, select c2: nearest cross is c1 (left), plus goes to c0 — empty. Select c4: nearest cross is c2 (left, distance 2), plus goes to c2 — on top of a cross! That might eliminate it?
Or maybe the plus is a "hint" showing where the cross will move if you press ACTION7 (move 2 in the direction of the nearest cross)?
Let me test: select c4 (19,36) and see where the plus appears. Prediction: nearest cross is c2 (distance 2, leftward) vs c5? Wait, is there a cross at c5 in row 1? No — the crosses in row 1 are c1, c2, c4. Row 2 has c5, row 4 has c5. Nearest cross to c4: c2 (distance 2). So the plus should appear at c2 (on top of the cross at c2). Let me verify.
Also, maybe I should test ACTION7 with a selection active to see what it does. But first, let me understand the plus mechanic with the c4 click.
Actually, let me think about what kind of game this is. 5 crosses, L-shaped board. The mechanic "click a cross → a ghost plus appears 2 blocks away in the direction of the nearest cross" strongly suggests a "push" mechanic: the selected cross will be pushed/moved 2 blocks in the direction of the nearest cross (like a slide), and the plus is a preview of the landing position. The goal is probably to move all crosses to... hmm, or to eliminate them.
Or this might be a "light" puzzle: the plus is a preview of where a "beam" will hit.
Let me test ACTION7 with the current selection (c2) and see what happens: does the cross at c2 move to c0 (where the plus is)? That would confirm the "move" hypothesis. But if I'm wrong, I might mess up the state. State seems to be reversible (clicking another cross moves the selection; maybe clicking the same cross deselects). Risk is acceptable.
Actually, the safer approach: first click c4 to check the plus prediction (a nearly read-only probe). Then test ACTION7.
